item.title: Permission to die
item.dc:creator: Aukkawut Ammartayakun
item.description:
Permission to die

Disclaimer

If you are asking “Am I OK?” or “How am I?”, the answer is “same as before”. Also please don’t contact emergency service on me. Last time I almost got raided by police if I were to not pick up my phone because someone thought I am in danger of harming myself. I found that quite funny but also, the police was ready to raid my apartment, literally.

Thinking about suicide is not the same as having suicide idealtion. Trust me, I did take psychopathology class and done a thesis on depression before.

This is somewhat a short essay but also not really. It is the same as my normal writing style and not intended to be academic style or your normal typical essay. Think of this as brain dump or shitpost.

Also, there are mentioning of Nazi stuff, I do not endorse them. I just have it there as an example.

What really is “permission”?

So, let’s start from the investigation of the phenomena that we observed it time to time: Ad hominem, an act of attacking person instead of their argument. Common word in academic, especially in philosophy. Fun question is: why is that a common word? If you are in academic world, you should be familiar with the concept of “attacking the argument, not the person”. Yes, in academic world. But, in real life? That is something that we see commonly. “Their face is the same as their thought” or “You should reduce your weight before talking about health”. Like, this is a normal discourse we see in the general non-academic discussion.

We can go on and discuss more on other fallacies. The point is, what gives them the right to say that? Well, free speech yes but I am not talking about that kind of right. I think I might need to go back to when I was in high school to illustrate this idea. So, a simple question, what makes people look “bully-able”? Say, you see obese person, do you have the thought of talking to them “fat” when they did something you don’t like? I am talking about that kind of “right”, or more so, “permission” to say that.

Or, what kind of speech or the way they talk makes you want to mock them for it? Because maybe it is not because of who they are, but how they view the world. Easiest way to see this is through the lens of political fraction. Suppose you support party A, which might be conservative. Then, what about party B, which can be liberal? I don’t think I need to explain further on how that will end up because I assume everyone reading this is familiar with said concept. If not, go read the news. Look at the comment on the news about protest. Or not even that, suppose we are talking in academic term, how to not get mocked by “influencer” or “gatekeeper” in that field just by explaining what you understand?

That essence of “what leads people into bullying” is what I meant by “permission”. What allows them to morally or logically justified their action that is, from the third-person perspective, is wrong? What traits resulting in suffering of the one who has that?

On suicide

Now, when people thinking about suicide, it is almost a taboo to not investigate on it from pessimism perspective. It is, as someone has said, horror of philosophy. It is common that people would say “there is too much to live for” as a motivation speech. Or “your life matters” and other similar phrases. Those mean nothing to the person who is suffering. It is like saying to the Sisyphus, “keep rolling, your rolling matters”. But it is also easy to say “just die your life does not matter” when you don’t even considering about the consequences or morality of death. Surprisingly, dying costs money. It causes suffering, specifically, to someone who wants you to stay alive.

That begs a lot of questions: “Is wanting someone to stay alive a selfish need to keep you from suffering yourself?” or “does medical staff actually care about you or just doesn’t want to get investigated?” and much more. The answer for those questions are not exactly easy to investigate. Not like we can think for others, but still, doesn’t prevent us from asking their motives. But if someone really care and want to commit suicide, that also raise another interesting question: “how to turn that motive, specifically against you, to be negative”?

Say, pick utilitarianism as a moral philosophy. Essentially, we want to maximize the welfare or happiness of everyone. If we are living in suffering, one could say, not living is better from hedonic calculus perspective. But, problem is, each individual of us are not independent. That is, if we were to commit suicide, you are reducing your suffering and you might get happy, but others will feel sad. How can we turn the suffering from others into their happiness? That is where the “permission to die” coming into the play.

Permission to die

Suppose we want to commit suicide, so we plan ahead by making everyone suffer from our existence. Not because we actually harm them physically or being an asshole, but being people who could, in theory, “bully-able”. That essence that causes people to be asshole towards you is what we want to justify our death. Once everyone is happy with our death, then we did a moral thing of maximizing the happiness. We manipulate them into thinking that our death is deserved so that no one will feel sad or have moral objection on our suicide. Well, at least from Bentham’s theory (hence, why hedonic calculus), and not necessary Mills’ theory on utilitarianism. As Mills might argue that this is no difference in comparison with making everyone drunk and call that “happiness”.

But that doesn’t stop us from asking crucial question that, while utilitarianism allows us to be pessimistic to that point (and also not), does that justify the morality of people who committed suicide? This is just one of the major moral philosophy paradigm and yet here we are having the hard time argue about it. If everyone are happy to not see you again, would leaving morally justifiable? If we manufacturing that said situation, would that be morally justifiable?

There is another concept that usually understate which is antinatalism. This is generally overshadowed by the right of abortion. If abortion is justifiable then why you are the one who invented that suffering in the first place? Why would we just not, you know, talk about antinatalism instead of abortion? Oh yes, 9 months are long enough to change the decision, but we argue that it doesn’t matter. Then, why does ending our lives are not the same? I changed my mind on living so I should have my right to, you know, end it. Why it has to be someone else who take the moral decision of you being alive or death? Like, that fetus doesn’t ask to be born in the first place, yet when they are now born, we say actually, no. Playing the role of god deciding whether they are alive or not because you don’t think it through in the first place. Yet, we, as a society, put the blame into the one who committed suicide as “not thinking it through”. Because abortion is not a taboo but suicide is a taboo, is that it?

If autonomy is sufficient to justify refusing continued existence before or after birth, then autonomy should carry significant weight in a competent person’s decision to end their own life. Yet, here we are in the society where “you should not die” but killing a fetus is OK. We are living in a society where we don’t have autonomy in our lives. We need permission to not exist to be morally acceptable. We need other people to allow us to die. Why can’t we just, simply, say good bye and be done? Why we have to entangled our lives with others to the point that dying is not an option? We say, your life is yours but put moral responsibility and burden into the one who suffered and want it to end. Clearly, we own our own life. But also, we embrace intervention for someone who just want to end it. We say that is not a right thing to do. Then, what is a right thing to do? Who dictates that?

Dying costs something. Clearly, one part is money to dispose your body. But also the burden on people who has to do it. Then, from this perspective, is burden of disposing or taking care of the mess something you want to avoid? Then, is that said burden the motivation for intervention? Or the burden of not having them “contribute to the society”? Or anything that justified your “keep going” mindset? Isn’t it the same as “you look bully-able”? Both are the same somehow. That is, one has special moral duty to intervene the person’s wish somehow. One is to not get bullied but well, “bully-able”. another one is “I want to end it” but well, “you have so much to live for”.

Can we exploit this mechanism so that, if we want to die, we can die? Would it still be moral if we exploit this chain? What is worth so much to live for and why that is morally superior to, end it all? What justifies the intervention and how can we make sure that doesn’t exists? How can we make ourselves into “deserved to die”? Say, would you kill Hitler because he did holocaust with his justification of something common at that time: antisemitism? What makes you think killing Hitler is OK? Do I have to be like Hitler to die? I am not saying Hitler is good, but at which point we say a person deserved to die? One can argue that Hitler radicalize the antisemitism and push it further. Not saying that is justifiable morally, but also if we think about it, was Hitler also a victim himself? It doesn’t erase the fact that he killed (through proxy and what not) a lot of people. It doesn’t erase the fact that he caused suffering to the entire world. But can a bad guy also a victim of the society where moral autonomy is just, not there? How much autonomy is required before another person may legitimately override your decision? Hitler had ability to stop, fix, and atone at anytime. He did not. He was a victim but also did not try to make it right. But interestingly, dying is one time thing. You die and it is ended, you can’t stop being dying. How can we be so gullible that we can just die? Is dying justifiable if we can’t fix it?

We are not on the binary decision on whether suicide is good or bad. But we are at the situation that, why can’t we just make a decision to ourselves through our autonomy and ability to think of it? How to minimize the consequence of dying so that it is justifiable to die? These are why “permission to die” is needed. What really is the moral basis of “suicide” and “suicide intervention”?

item.title: UTK Eduroam on terminal
item.dc:creator: Aukkawut Ammartayakun
item.description:
Connecting to UTK’s eduroam in Linux (CLI)

Origin of this

Well, let me start with the experience I got talking to IT.

  • I don’t know how to connect to eduroam (in a sense that I don’t know how they set it up) via iwd on my Linux.
  • Check the KB (knowledge base) page and there is no section for Linux when connecting into eduroam
  • Went to walk-in tech support. They don’t even know what I am doing in tty (showing them I need config file, but I don’t know format used here at UTK)
  • They call technician, they look at it and try to open setting (which is setting for desktop environment (Enlightenment), not for Wi-Fi. I mean, I did told them I use iwd and iwctl to connect)
  • They ask is this Windows or Mac. Told them it is Linux. They ask is this Ubuntu, I told them it is Gentoo. They don’t know that and they said sorry we only support Windows and Mac.
  • Figuring it out from CMU blog
  • Try it on my local Gentoo laptop from 2010 (that, surprisingly, has a hardware that support it). It works.
  • Send a ticket to IT to update their KB to be inclusive to Linux user who doesn’t use GUI (like a typical person) to connect to Wi-Fi.

I am a bit mad because if they don’t know their system configuration, then who is supposed to know? I understand the support part because it will be hell if you support all operating systems. However, I do think that it is still their responsibility to at least tell how the network is setup technically

Just to be clear, I don’t mind not knowing. I understand the load of their work. It is just that I feel dissapointed on how they handle my problem. And it seems like ticket is lost (or they are doing something with it, I don’t know) but here I am writing on what I tried and works.

How to connect

Official way

Well, just use https://cat.eduroam.org/ script. Problem is, it might not fit with what your system has (like I did).

iwd

This is what I did. The solution is simple, I use the method from this blog by Gautam Iyer at CMU.

  1. Create file /var/lib/iwd/eduroam.8021x (or in directory iwd store new connection)
  2. In that file, add
[Security]
EAP-Method=PEAP
EAP-Identity=<netid>@vols.utk.edu
EAP-PEAP-Phase2-Method=MSCHAPV2
EAP-PEAP-Phase2-Identity=<netid>@vols.utk.edu

Obviously, change vols.utk.edu to utk.edu or domain you use and you should be good to go.

wpa_supplicant

Well, I will test it soon and will update this.

Update: I leave the university so I don’t know what is the configuration but I think it is on the similar manner.

item.title: Gentoo Experience
item.dc:creator: Aukkawut Ammartayakun
item.description:
Gentoo and Old Tech Experience

So, it has been like 2 months (more or less) since I first start installed and change my life to Gentoo linux. At first, people don’t believe me that I use Linux or tinkering with old laptops. Surprisingly, I did. Here is the story and how I see it.

Starting Point

Why Old Tech?

You know, I live in the world that people labeled me as “Gen-Z”. Typical stereotype of Gen-Z is that we live in the world full of technology, like the modern technology. That is partially true if you are late Gen-Z. Sadly, I was born and live with Windows 95. I use a lot of Windows XP, 7, 8, 8.1, 10, and 11 as I am growing up (Vista, not so much).

I was born with CRT screen, sony beta cam, and a lot of tech people called it “old”. Home computer was just a starting point back then and not widely popular due to its cost and other setup (like ISP, hardware shipping, etc.) You know, we don’t have good shipping system back then so if you live in a bit of rural area (like I did), only way to get computer is either from local company or tech shop nearby.

I was not a computer nerd back then. I know how to use computer and I can say I know a lot more than typical people. But I would say because I know how to read tech manual better than the other than actual skill. I know how to read in English (but not how to write properly, sadly). I like computer because it is flashy and cool back then. Like, I can talk to my sister who study aboard via Skype and MSN (or QQ).

Back then, if we want to use cool webcam, we have that. If we want to talk to stranger online, use camfrog. If you want to roleplay? Try Forum. You have all the forum you want ranges from tech support, selling stuff, to Harry Potter roleplay, alumni forum of some school, etc. You can Google it (or heck, use “hub” website like Yahoo! or Kapook to get to where you want).

Can’t deny that those are one of the fun memory I have in life. Sadly, as some of you might already know, my life in childhood was not the best. I got bullied a lot in middle and high school. My first laptop which is netbook was stolen by one of the student during my middle school. Teachers and staff did nothing about it and pretend it never happened. I got physical assults from people in there a lot and a lot of psychological hazing. My life was shit back then.

The only few happy memories I have tied with the computer. I did a lot of robotics back in middle and high school as an escape route to have time to myself.

Using Linux was also one of the experience I try to distract myself from the painful reality. In fact, I know Linux since primary school from national opeating system: Suriyan. One of the rep give me the disc full of educational software and Tux games. I was happy back then to explore all of those.

Then, in my middle school, I started to use Linux more often. I used to daily drive with Ubuntu back then. I would change the font to national font “TH-SarabunPSK” and feel like a cool kids. But alas, as a kid, I do have urge to play game and back then, Linux was shit for gaming. So, I undeniably need to move to Windows to play game.

In high school, I went back to Linux again when my computer is broken, it was a good time tinkering with GTK and stuff. Then, it is the start of the old tech arc of my life. I started to buy old Macbook off eBay and play with it.

I was surprised that it has Python installed in it back then. It is like a spark in my brain to look back again and think about it.

Linux Transition

Well, I use linux a lot when I was first start to know about CTF. There was a cool CTF called picoCTF where you are supposed to “find” the hidden flag by completing the objective like finding hidden string in the image, or pwning the system using canary stuff. Or reverse engineering the pseudo random number generation algorithm to retrieve the passcode, or even to render SSTV stuff.

I used Windows back then because, duh I play game. Problem is, it requires a lot of shell command that I need to resort to the competition webshell instead of my own computer. That is the start of my Linux arc. Again, I use Ubuntu because it was something I used to.

I use that to complete the assignment up to the college, while still have Windows PC lying around for gaming. I used Parrot OS on old iMac I auctioned from the eBay. Then, COVID hit. All of my computer were lost because I need to go back to my home country during the break without packing up the stuff.

So, the start of the college is when I need Ubuntu machine for “Data Science” assignment. Well, I will say GPU support back then was fine but not the best. I learned a lot about hardware and driver and low-level stuff (beside C that I usually code with already).

Other than using Ubuntu, MacOS, or computer cluster, I treat Linux as “work” system as I am a game addicted.

Full Linux Experience

Time goes by and now I am Ph.D student. I am suffering from burnout as I rush through the program (got undergrad and master at the same time within 4 years, 21 credits almost every semesters, 4 theses at the end). I found that old tech is really interesting. Old tech is like, me. It is capable, but deem obsolete by other people just because I am slow from my burnout.

I then started to buy old computer one by one. I heard that BunsenLabs is one of the lean system so I use that on my first computer: emachine em250. Well, it is 32 bits machine so I use Bunsenlabs. Hey, it works. Just still slow.

Then, I decided to use Arch Linux because it sounds like a light system. I use Arch32, the one with no archinstall script. Oh well, it is my first time I need to learn about how Linux works really. But more like, what components are required to make a workable Linux environment.

I need to format my drive, partition it, and install minimal basic system, chroot and install the rest, then install bootloader, and done.

To be honest, Arch Linux is easier to use and is intuitive. I am surprised that the “hard-to-use” system is really not that hard, but I can see why people suffer with it. It is indeed light! Can be lighter without xfce of course, but I want full desktop because I am too lazy. Then, it hits me, the way to make this even lighter!

Then, I started to buy more old laptop and more. And alas, Gentoo Linux is where I am going next. I heard that Gentoo is notorious operating system yet should be able to run on any (reasonable) hardware that can compile code. Mine does, so why not give it a try?

I installed everything and compile everything myself. It is 32 bits so there is no like binary package really. I did not setup crossdev or something similar because I am completely new to this. It took me a week to get the running system with this FVWM. I hate compiling llvm stuff so much yet I need it for xorg-server. It was a pain watching this Intel Atom N270 scream to death.

But you know what? It does run fast and snappy. I feel great about my system. I listen to radio using this machine and try to daily drive with it so it force me to tune the system or make it fast enough for daily use. I learned about USE flag and optimization a lot through this machine. So much so that I tuned a lot of stuff to my liking yet forget to add random number generation to the kernel option.

I probably will left it there and update it during the break. But hey, learning new things, troubleshooting stuff, fix stuff, and tune stuff actually help with my burnout. It is like a hobby per se, where I can enjoy challenging myself with the problem in there. As you can see, I can read PDF just fine on this computer or use Canvas and stuff.

Now, the second computer in the list is Panasonic Toughbook CF-C1. Damn this is one of my favorite computer. It is x86_64 computer so binary binary binary. I use oddlama/gentoo-install script to install kernel on this one because I am too lazy. But alas, I need to manually install the system myself anyway because I mess it up again and again tuning it.

For this computer, I mostly try different DE like Enlightenment,xfce or the typical WM like FVWM. I honestly like both DEs but now lean more towards just WM. Then, I found myself want to fully daily drive the Linux, including my main Workstation I used to play game with. So, I install Gentoo on my main computer.

Damn, it is fast and snappy. There is no problematic Windows update stuff or any silly Windows thing. Just what I want. I can tune and tinker everything, use anything I want. And now I can play game using proton from Steam. I feel like I am alive daily driving this. Of course, compiling stuff take time but this is my powerhouse so I can just go to bathroom or walk outside, come back, and everything is done.

Nvidia is not a problem either, Gentoo surprisingly make it easy to install those driver compared to other Distro (as per my old experience). It is seamless and I have no problem installing driver.

Meditation on Old Tech

Maybe me tinkering on this old laptop is a way I converse with myself. Maybe it is just me trying to tell myself that I am the embodiment of this laptop that still functioning, but we deep down know that at this point I am burning it out.

It is like I try to fix myself, holding myself together when the world is demanding more and more. This machine is still capable, yes. But it really need to push effort to just meet the same level as other hardware. It can visit many websites or even youtube, but the world just ignore this old machine. We say it is obsolete and makes website and application more absurd.

We make expectation for a person. And that expectation is more absurd and absurd that there is no human left in there. We forget that human exists. We see it as a machine, as this computer that either being e-waste or need to meed absurd standard.

I don’t know how long I can hold myself together. Maybe in the end I might just be e-waste. Not fast enough for modern standard. Does not support modern instructions. Low memory with old hard drive. Can’t just get binaries and need to compile and build software from scratch. Power hungry and doesn’t hold much charge on batteries.

It just take one loose connection or one capacitor to explode to make people ditch it without looking at it. It is too old why bother? It is e-waste at this point why fix it? The world does not wait. People does not wait. It can easily run optimization ir even Monte Carlo simulation if you give them time and care, but why bother on this obsolete tech when we have better one?

Final Remark

This is more or less brain dump than the good blog, I might come back and tune it a bit. However, this is really my gentoo experience. It is damn fast, damn snappy. I learned a lot, and I feel like I have full control over my computer. Other distros does not give me this, not even Arch Linux. Community is nice if you know where to talk to (some are still elitists like Arch, but more welcome compared to Arch in my opinion).

Handbook is really nice touch but I learned a hard way to not treat that as a holy grail, but to treat it as a guideline and do what you have to do with your hardware (on my emachine, I can’t compile kernel following the direction verbatim, but I need to deivate a bit to fix problems here and there to compile the kernel). That is what you should expect: solving the problem, rather than to think that guide is seamless.
